svg.text: The same core as the server edition, living inside your process — no TCP, no daemon, no DynamoDB. Only the coordination and storage corners differ; Nexus and CHASM have their own diagrams.

text.tspan: Solid arrows: synchronous flow. Dashed: control / async.
Numbered badges reference the annotation panel.
Lane: blake3 hash of the run key.
Send LaneMessage to the lane channel.

svg.text: Per-run serialization by construction: same run key ⇒ same lane ⇒ sequential processing.

text.tspan: timers · wf/wft/activity timeouts · grace · drain · fairness · heartbeat · nexus · callbacks. Most re-enter via lanes;
activity timeouts commit off-lane through their own OCC loop — the second mutation door.

svg.text: Brokers — WFT + activity (Nexus → its own diagram)

text.tspan: Tier A: sync-match on eager start → instant handoff.
Tier B: live-ready in-memory queues (sticky beside general).
Tier C: durable backlog — demote/rehydrate lives in backlog.rs.
Key: namespace / task queue / kind / deployment / build_id.
Commit 2 · Read 1 · Proj 1 · Ctrl 1 · Maint 3 — ratios × target_ready(8)
Embedded reservoir: deadline-aware warmup + shutdown · leak detector — no DynamoDB
in-memory (default) · managed Aurora DSQL · adopted Aurora DSQL
snapshots are a policy, not a mode: optional on in-memory — restore at boot,
periodic + shutdown capture. tokeira-managed-dsql owns the cluster lifecycle.
Edge mutation enters Runtime.submit; this is the only entry
ShardOwner gates admission. Inactive/draining shards fail
fast; edge invalidates routing and retries.
A run key hashes to exactly one lane — local per-run
Lane channel is bounded; backpressure is explicit rather than
handle_message loads state and commits transitions through
OCC conflicts retry on the lane (max 5); reply is sent only
tokeira-kernel is pure: LoadedRun + Command → Transition, no
History, timers, and the visibility snapshot commit in one
fenced transaction; only dispatch publishes after.
9–11 · Brokers handle poll matching and WFT start dispatch
History reads bypass lanes and read committed history directly
13–15 · Loops re-enter via lanes — except activity timeouts,
which commit off-lane: the drawn second door.
16–18 · The process-local budget and the control lease replace
DynamoDB; durable broker fallback is unchanged.
One process owns every shard; the DSQL control lease is
the exclusion authority — fenced on every checkout.
Snapshot rows ride the commit; consuming them lags freely —
projection lag cannot change workflow truth.
